jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT STRAVA

Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey https://www.strava.com/subscription with Strava today.

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is a high-impact opportunity to drive the financial picture behind one of Strava's most important growth areas at a pivotal moment in the company's journey. As Strava scales toward its next chapter as a global consumer subscription business, you'll shape how we understand and invest behind a core part of the business, partnering with senior leaders and building the analysis behind the company's most important financial decisions.

The role sits within the Product Finance pillar of our FP&A team, which partners with leaders across the business to guide the company's growth. The pillar covers the core drivers of Strava Group's financial performance, with a primary focus on revenue and marketing investments.

As part of the Product Finance team within FP&A, you will drive the analysis behind a core part of Strava's subscription business — building and maintaining the revenue models, monitoring performance, and developing the recommendations that inform how the forecast is set. You will partner closely with key stakeholders across the business — including teammates across our San Francisco and London offices — to translate data into clear, actionable insight, and you will give senior leadership visibility into the trends that shape the business, with the opportunity to influence decisions at the executive level.

We follow a flexible hybrid model that translates to more than half of your time on-site in our San Francisco office, three days per week. This role includes occasional travel to London on an as-needed basis (approximately twice a year).




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Serve as a key finance partner for a core area of the business, building deep fluency in its drivers and acting as a trusted point of contact for its leadership and cross-functional teams

 - Monitor and analyze business performance, identify trends, and translate findings into clear recommendations for senior management

 - Build and maintain driver-based financial models across multiple time horizons

 - Drive visibility into core business trends for senior leadership, influencing decisions at the executive level

 - Partner cross-functionally to turn financial analysis into strategic decisions, surfacing performance and investment trade-offs for key stakeholders




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - 4+ years of experience in finance or a related analytical field, such as corporate finance, investment banking, private equity, or management consulting

 - Exceptional cross-functional partnership and coordination skills, including experience keeping distributed stakeholders aligned across time zones (our London office is a key partner to this role)

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with experience building and maintaining driver-based models

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex financial information for a range of audiences

 - A self-starter who thrives in ambiguity, takes ownership, and manages competing priorities in a high-growth environment



For information on benefits, please click here https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vTkFMPz3eCjd0FgQ28VWnK4d2BEnzGyaSFGwATR-dQdBb9HxZgay6kboqnT0-V-qaBDzSvYIzI76vT5/pub.




WHY JOIN US?



Movement brings us together. At Strava, we’re building the world’s largest community of active people, helping them stay motivated and achieve their goals.

Our global team is passionate about making movement fun, meaningful, and accessible to everyone. Whether you’re shaping the technology, growing our community, or driving innovation, your work at Strava makes an impact.

When you join Strava, you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a movement. If you’re ready to bring your energy, ideas, and drive, let’s build something incredible together.

Strava builds software that makes the best part of our athletes’ days even better. Just as we’re deeply committed to unlocking their potential, we’re dedicated to providing a world-class, inclusive workplace where our employees can grow and thrive, too. We’re backed by Sequoia Capital, TCV, Madrone Partners and Jackson Square Ventures, and we’re expanding in order to exceed the needs of our growing community of global athletes. Our culture reflects our community. We are continuously striving to hire and engage teammates from all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives because we know we are a stronger team together.

Strava is an equal opportunity employer. In keeping with the values of Strava, we make all employment decisions including hiring, evaluation, termination, promotional and training opportunities, without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, physical handicap, mental disability, medical condition, disability, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight.

jobs.description:

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.



About This Role

We're looking for a Director, Strategic Sourcing & Procurement to stand up the Procurement function at Strava! You will be the person who designs all of it: the operating model, the commercial strategy, the systems—and then runs it. This is a unique opportunity for those passionate about creating systems and processes from scratch.

A key part of this role will be personally negotiating our largest agreements and carrying a savings target agreed with FP&A. You should feel confident bringing analytical rigor to commercial negotiations, know how to restructure a deal to achieve multiple objectives, and be comfortable holding a position despite pushback from senior stakeholders. The majority of your work will be infrastructure spend and B2B SaaS. But the scope of responsibility covers all material areas of spend, including agencies and professional services. This role reports to the General Counsel and is based in our San Francisco office. 



We follow a flexible hybrid model that translates to more than half of your time on-site in our San Francisco office — three days per week. 



What You'll Do:

 - Stand up the Procurement function, defining the operating model, policy, thresholds, and decision rights that govern how Strava buys.

 - Build and lead the team, starting by hiring and developing a Manager, Procurement Operations, and shaping how the function grows from there.

 - Own a named portfolio of our largest agreements, leading negotiations personally and holding accountability for commercial outcomes.

 - Carry a hard savings target, with a baseline methodology agreed with FP&A.

 - Establish renewal calendar discipline across the portfolio, engaging early enough on major agreements to create genuine leverage.

 - Develop a negotiation playbook, benchmarking approach, and escalation criteria.

 - Partner with Legal on contracting, Finance on budget and savings validation, and IT and Security on vendor review, keeping all tracks running in parallel rather than in series.

 - Drive vendor rationalization across the long tail, identifying overlap, underused licenses, and consolidation opportunities.

 - Give leadership clear, credible visibility into what we spend, with whom, and what we're getting for it. 



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - The instinct of a builder. You are energized rather than daunted by an empty org chart and an undefined process.

 - Genuine commercial rigor. You treat a negotiation as an enjoyable analytical problem and know how to strategically leverage every position.

 - Judgment and standing to hold a position under pressure, and the relationship skills to do so without becoming an obstacle people route around.

 - Proactively spotting potential issues and taking initiative to resolve them, understanding that "nothing is somebody else's problem."

 - A collaborative, no-task-is-beneath-me approach to your work. 

 - Professionalism without ego. 



Requirements:

 - 10+ years experience building a procurement or strategic sourcing function

 - Substantial experience negotiating enterprise B2B SaaS and technology agreements, with a demonstrable record of Finance-validated commercial improvement.

 - People management experience, including hiring, developing, and retaining team members.

 - Fluency translating spend data into a commercial narrative for executive audiences.

 - Exposure to public company or pre-IPO purchasing controls, segregation of duties, and audit requirements.

 - Confidence using modern tools and systems (e.g., Zip, Ironclad, Slack, Notion, AI) to amplify impact.

 - Own brand media measurement planning and strategy, ensuring investments align directly with Strava’s brand marketing OKRs – proactively identifying and proposing strategic improvements to measurement frameworks across the team and key partners.

You'll own the application and continuous refinement of our measurement methodology stack, making informed decisions that balance short-term reporting needs with long-term measurement objectives.

 - Drive alignment across teams by gathering requirements from partners across the organization, collaborating to ensure alignment and maximize impact on measurement capabilities that complement their workflows.

 - Deliver persuasive and data-driven media performance reviews, translating complex findings into clear, compelling narratives that inform and drive decisions at the weekly and monthly business reviews.

 - Provide the “source of truth” for internal consumers by owning critical analytical reporting on metrics like aided brand awareness, familiarity, and consideration. You take ownership of these strategic initiatives and drive them forward with minimal guidance.

 - Apply expertise in brand health surveys, including the statistics behind sampling and reporting results, to proactively identify and address gaps before they impact decision-making.

 - Create and manage data pipelines from multiple sources, leading the design of scalable, performant ETL workflows that keep data accessible, fresh, and consistent — and mentoring teammates on technical best practices.

 - Collaborate with Strava's broader data organization (Machine Learning, Data Platform, and beyond), demonstrating determination to collectively improve our technological craftsmanship, even when navigating ambiguous or complex challenges.

 - You have 5+ years of full-time experience in analytics, data science, or other quantitative domains supporting growth marketing teams, and have a track record of independently executing large-scale measurement projects and initiatives.

 - You have 3+ years of experience with performance measurement across paid and organic channels, including TikTok, Meta, Reddit, and similar platforms and can anticipate and evaluate risks and opportunities associated with cross-channel strategies to make informed recommendations.

 - You have a track record of defining and building the key metrics and dimensions that accurately reflect user behavior and drive meaningful marketing decisions, proactively taking on challenging assignments and driving them to completion with strong organizational alignment.

 - You are highly skilled in SQL, with extensive experience extracting large datasets and designing ETL workflows that balance performance and scalability, and you bring the analytical rigor to identify the right solutions to complex, ambiguous problems.

 - You're proficient in quantitative programming languages like Python, experienced with Tableau, consistently seeking to initiate improvements to processes and tools that deliver superior results.

 - You are comfortable operating in ambiguity — able to design the right test, identify the best proxy metric, or transparently frame uncertainty in a way that empowers decision-makers rather than stalls them.

 - You bring deep technical expertise in brand measurement methodologies, including Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), brand lift studies, and experimental design.

 - You take high ownership of your work, collaborating proactively with partners across the business to ensure alignment, maximize impact, and drive continuous improvement.

 - You're a strong communicator who can craft compelling narratives and ensure transparency by proactively sharing relevant insights that could impact projects or decisions.

 - You consistently meet goals, keep projects on pace, and follow through on your commitments, demonstrating the ability to analyze and prioritize projects based on their potential impact and maintain momentum even in challenging circumstances.

jobs.title: Retention Marketing Manager, GTM & Feature Adoption
jobs.description:
ABOUT STRAVA

Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey https://www.strava.com/subscription with Strava today.

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.



About This Role

Strava's Retention team is responsible for reinforcing ongoing subscription value, from renewal to feature adoption, through lifecycle marketing and experimentation. As Product's GTM velocity has grown, so has the need for a dedicated bridge between Product Marketing (PMM) and Lifecycle Marketing, so that new launches can be supported by one-off activations, as well as integrated into lifecycle programs. 



This role owns that bridge. You'll represent Retention across GTM alignment forums with PMM, MarTech, and Data, translating GTM briefs into scoped plans, targetable audiences, and experiment designs, and project managing each launch from creative handover through post-campaign analysis.  You'll partner closely with individual lifecycle marketers to route GTM opportunities into existing lifecycle programs where it makes sense, and to build new, repeatable ones where it doesn't. You're the first dedicated hire in this new pod, so you'll be hands-on from day one: running launches end to end, building them yourself in our martech stack, and shaping the first working version of the playbook as you go. 



We follow a flexible hybrid model that translates to more than half of your time on-site in our San Francisco or New York City office, three days per week. 



What You'll Do:

 - Represent Retention in ongoing GTM alignment forums across PMM, MarTech, and Data, owning brief intake and early-stage scoping so success metrics are defined before a GTM kicks off.

 - Drive the GTM channel strategy and experimentation plan end to end: align stakeholders, confirm launch dates and experimentation design, review first-round creative, and manage the project from creative handover through post-campaign analysis.

 - Translate GTM briefs into targetable audience lists, partnering with MarTech to identify what's available and close data gaps, so PMM can size launches accurately.

 - Design and run incremental A/B tests on GTM campaigns, defining success metrics and mapping results against PMM's and Retention's learning agendas.

 - Meet regularly with lifecycle marketers to understand their quarterly goals and surface GTM opportunities in that context, handing off strategic ownership on higher-tier programs to the marketer who owns that history, and owning execution directly on lower-tier tests.

 - Bridge Product Engineering, PMM, and MarTech tooling (Iterable, Braze, Kevel) to enable the right data into comms systems, and build, QA, and launch GTM campaigns in our martech stack.

 - Apply PMM's tiering structure to run launches consistently, log results against a shared benchmark set so comparing campaigns stops being one-off reporting, and informs how the next launch gets scoped.

 - Support seasonal and brand-led campaigns (e.g., major marathon upsells, gifting and family plan moments, back-to-school promotions) with owned-channel strategy and execution. 



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 4-6 years of hands-on experience across growth, lifecycle, or product marketing, with fluency in both worlds: you can shape briefs collaboratively with PMM and connect GTMs into existing lifecycle programs

 - A track record of designing and running experiments: defining success metrics, structuring fair tests, and translating results into clear recommendations. 

 - Excellent project management skills: you can manage multiple concurrent launches end to end and keep cross-functional partners aligned on timelines and dependencies.

 - Experience partnering with data or engineering teams to translate marketing briefs into targetable audiences and flag data gaps early.

 - A builder's mindset: you're motivated by setting something up from scratch and improving it launch over launch.

 - Hands-on experience building and QAing campaigns in marketing automation or ad-serving platforms (such as Iterable, Braze, or Kevel).

 - Familiarity with subscription or freemium business models is a plus. 

 

How This Role Grows

The role is deliberately hands-on to start: you'll be running launches, building them yourself, and finding out what works. As the pod matures, so does the scope — from running each launch yourself to owning the system others run them through. That means codifying how GTMs get executed and measured, turning one-off activations into a repeatable playbook, and holding senior relationships across Product and PMM directly. It's a path we've mapped rather than implied, and part of why we're hiring this role now rather than later.

Our global team is passionate about making movement fun, meaningful, and accessible to everyone. Whether you’re shaping the technology, growing our community, or driving innovation, your work at Strava makes an impact.
